threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’ve still got the plastic cover on your new coffee table from IKEA. Everyone else here has embraced the vintage vibe by now.
Last night on the 68, a bloke serenaded us with Mobb Deep tracks. Even the driver was vibing. Brixton nights are never dull.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a toddler collecting fallen leaves with a hipster in a café, while a street performer played chanson next to a yoga class in the park.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst at 3 AM after a night of dancing, while the Döner shop next door gives you side eye for being too mainstream.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their unbothered stroll past the dodging pigeons near Dolores Park, while newcomers are still dodging the techies on scooters.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on a Muni bus while the driver was trying to fix a broken fare box. The whole ride turned into a weird circus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think our plazas are just for photos, but locals actually catch up over vermut there, with the kids running wild around the fountains.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their hesitant thumbs-up to the street performers; locals just nod and keep walking.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘Stokey’ is a cute nickname instead of a sign you’ve got the drink culture all wrong. We call it 'Stoke Newington' for a reason!
Last night, someone brought a full drum kit on the 196. By the time we got to Stockwell, they had a whole jam session going on.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I walked past the record shop and heard a street musician playing the same obscure track I had on vinyl. Felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a tram rolling down the street, completely ignoring the traffic lights, while cyclists whiz by in their own anarchic lanes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays; they’ve got a backup route ready while newcomers just stand confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus while another passenger recited Shakespeare. Only in the TL can a ride feel like a live show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm lies in its hidden plazas and local tapas bars that echo with laughter, not just tourists.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still pull out a map in Plaça del Sol, while the rest of us just look for the nearest bar.
